svg.title: Conditions and complications among people with diabetes in the United States
svg.desc: In 2021–23, 76.4% of U.S. adults with diagnosed diabetes had hypertension or used blood pressure medication, 41.7% had chronic kidney disease stages 1–4, and 38.0% had non-HDL cholesterol of at least 130 mg/dL. Among all U.S. people with diabetes in 2021, 26.43% had diabetic retinopathy. In 2025, 8.8% of U.S. adults with diagnosed diabetes reported a history of stroke. In 2023 there were 7.30 hospital stays involving lower-limb amputation per 1,000 U.S. adults with diagnosed diabetes.
svg.metadata: Adapted from Mikael Häggström, Male template with organs and Female template with organs (Wikimedia Commons, CC0 1.0). Diabetes data sources and denominators are identified in the report.
svg.text: U.S. people with diabetes, all ages, 2021.
